title: cost-lab-runner-and-quant-safeguard-prototyper
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: teams increasingly want a low-risk sandbox to evaluate tenant-level unit economics changes (batching, cache defaults, and aggressive quantization) before applying them to production. This PR introduces a lightweight "Cost Lab" runner service plus an experimental Quant Safeguard Advisor designed to run isolated what-if experiments, score end-to-end token/unit cost impacts, and produce safe fallback-presets. High-level summary: add a new microservice (cmd/cost-lab-runner) that orchestrates tenant-specific synthetic workloads, a simulator library (pkg/econ/simulator) that replays request traces with configurable batching and cache policies, and a quant sensitivity probe (pkg/quant/safeguard) that performs operator-level pruning experiments and synthesizes robust quantization ladders constrained by latency SLOs and fallthrough quality thresholds. The PR also exposes a small CLI (tools/costlab-cli) for offline dry-runs and a console toggle (web/console/src/components/CostLabToggle.tsx) to seed canary experiments. Key behavior: experiments run against a sandboxed runtime instance with prefix/KV caching disabled by default; the runner supports multi-tenant trace slices, deterministic random seeds for repeatability, and automated scoring metrics (token-cost delta, P95 latency delta, model-quality proxy using saved prompt/eval pairs). Safety & rollout: generated presets are annotated with confidence scores and suggested rollout policies (canary fraction, warmup duration). The advisor will never auto-apply presets; it emits a diffs-as-code artifact that can be reviewed and applied by operators. Implementation notes: most of the heavy work is encapsulated in pkg/econ/simulator and pkg/quant/safeguard so the change surface for the serving runtime is minimal (a small agent hook at internal/runtime/experiment_agent.go to shadow traffic). Telemetry: new metrics and tags added under telemetry.econ.* and telemetry.quant.*; we included sample Grafana dashboard JSON under observability/dashboards/cost-lab.json. Testing: unit tests for simulator determinism and quant probe stability included (pkg/econ/simulator/sim_test.go, pkg/quant/safeguard/safeguard_test.go). An e2e smoke harness (tests/e2e/costlab_smoke.sh) runs in CI. Performance: microbenchmarks show the simulation harness runs 6-8x faster than a naive replayer due to batched trace replay and compiled kernel selection toggles; we include a perf-run report in docs/perf/costlab_run_2026-01.pdf. Backwards compatibility: all defaults are conservative; no changes to user-facing inference defaults without opt-in. Followups: integrate the advisor with Optimize to propose one-click preset migrations and add a model-quality regression detector for high-risk quant ladders. Why different from previous work: this change packages simulation + quant pruning into a discoverable, sandbox-first developer flow (Cost Lab) rather than a purely autosuggesting default generator. It is intended for advanced SRE/ML-ops experimentation workflows.

feat(simulator): deterministic trace replayer with batching and cache knobs
feat(quant): implement operator sensitivity probe and quant-ladder synthesizer
chore(cli): add costlab-cli for offline dry-runs and result export
feat(console): add Cost Lab toggles and experiment summary panel
test: add unit and e2e smoke tests; add CI e2e job
docs: add dashboard and perf report; update runbook
fix: tighten sandbox networking and add timeout guards
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Overall design looks solid. Two requests: (1) ensure experiment_agent cannot leak tensors to prod caches, (2) add a CLI flag to force deterministic seed. Reply (Maya): both addressed in latest commits; agent sanitizes all KV writes and seed flag added.
Priya Patel: Can you add a short section to the runbook describing how to validate model-quality proxies? Reply (Maya): added 'validating-proxies' section in docs/runbooks/cost-lab-runbook.md.

Diego Marquez: Suggest adding a fallback policy when quant ladder leads to >5% P95 regression. Reply (Maya): added confidence score and a suggested 'auto-fallback' policy in the diff artifact; it remains opt-in for operators.
ci_checks: perf-bench: flaky on first run (re-run passed)
release_notes: Introduce Cost Lab runner: sandboxed experiment harness for tenant-level what-if analysis (batching, cache, quantization)
Add Quant Safeguard Advisor: operator-level quant pruning experiments with confidence scores and diffs-as-code
Expose CLI and console toggles for canary experiments; conservative opt-in defaults
testing: unit: simulator determinism and quant prober stability (pkg/*_test.go)
e2e: costlab_smoke.sh covers a full synthetic tenant replay and artifact export
perf: microbench harness under docs/perf shows optimized replay speed
rollout_plan: stage 1: deploy Cost Lab binary to sandbox lane only; no production traffic affected
stage 2: enable canary toggle for 2 internal tenants and run predefined trace suites for 48h
stage 3: surface diffs to operators via Console and allow manual apply with suggested rollout policy
rollback: all presets are labelled and can be reverted; experiment_agent can be disabled via a runtime flag
